summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against every clause of the selected Greek. Neither presents a concrete fidelity defect. Both preserve the sleeping detail, rejected Sibyl identification, Church’s first-created status, world-order assertion, denial of delivering the book, the woman’s completion of the words, disclosure through Hermas to all the elect, and the distinct recipients and distribution tasks. The simplified sentence divisions preserve these relationships. The notes accurately disclose the supplied reports’ relevant alternatives, corrector distinctions, bracketed letters, conjectural wording, and mediated Ethiopic evidence without replacing the working reading or treating editorial supplements as preserved text. Acceptance is limited to source fidelity and disclosure against the supplied material; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or editions, certify exhaustive collation, or establish a unique interpretation.
